title: Add deployment-policy note to group-chat admin role wording
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md
Lines: 442, 881 (and adjacent context if needed)

Current text:
  Line 442: "For group chats, only admins may modify this list." (pinnedMessageIds)
  Line 881: "For group chats, admins additionally may update: name, description, avatarBlobId."

This is the odd Tier 3 item out: the fix isn't MUST → SHOULD because there is no MUST here. Both sentences describe what the `"admin"` role enum *means* in group chats. The two-role admin/member model is a deliberate tier distinction (group chats vs. channel chats in Spaces) and the role enum is wire-observable — generalizing it would collapse two tiers and break federation behavior.

But the spec is currently silent about whether deployments may map ADDITIONAL internal principals to the same admin authority. A deployment may legitimately want:
- A server administrator who can pin any message in any group chat
- An enterprise moderator with admin-equivalent authority delegated by directory service
- An automated cleanup system that prunes pinned messages on a schedule

None of these need a new wire-level role; they just act "as if" they were a member with the `"admin"` role. The spec should say this explicitly so implementers don't think they're constrained to the literal two-role model internally.

Suggested addition (a new paragraph in the group-chat creation section near line 873, or in a dedicated note near the ChatMember.role definition at line 369):

  "The `"admin" | "member"` role enum on `ChatMember` is the wire-observable representation of group-chat authority and is what remote peers see via {{JMAP-CHAT-FED}}. Servers MAY designate additional internal principals (server administrators, members of a dedicated moderator role, automated maintenance systems, or principals delegated by an external identity provider) as having admin-equivalent authority for the actions admins may perform; the means of designating such principals is deployment-defined. From a remote peer's perspective, all such administrative actions appear to originate from a member with the `"admin"` role on the originating server."

This bead is the natural follow-up that should NOT be conflated with we5b.2 (group-chat creator bootstrap). They share surface area but address different concerns:
- we5b.2: who STARTS as admin at creation (impl-defined, paralleling Space governance)
- This bead: whether deployments may have richer internal models behind the wire-observable admin role (yes, with an explanatory note)

Both can be true simultaneously; both should land. They are most easily reviewed as separate commits.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new paragraph (or note) appears in the main draft naming the deployment-policy latitude
- The wire-observable nature of the `"admin"` role enum is explicit
- Examples of internal principals (server admin, moderator role, automated system, external IdP) are listed as non-normative
- The federation observability statement (remote peers see actions as originating from admin) is explicit
- Lines 442 and 881 themselves are NOT modified; the new note is what does the work
- The bead does not blur into we5b.2's scope (which is about who starts as admin at creation, not about who else may act with admin-equivalent authority)
